newsitem.title: USA: Michigan gives Ameritech long-distance okay.
newsitem.headline: Michigan gives Ameritech long-distance okay.

text.p: Ameritech Corp won an important endorsement Wednesday from state regulators in Michigan in its efforts to become the first Baby Bell to offer long-distance phone service from its local-calling region.

The Michigan Public Service Commission advised the Federal Communications Commission that it appears Ameritech has met a 14-point checklist detailing that the Chicago-based carrier had opened its local phone network in Michigan to new competitors.
The checklist was spelled out under last year's big telecommunications law.

The FCC will make the final determination on whether Ameritech has indeed met the checklist for entry into the $78 billion long-distance market. But a negative recommendation from Michigan would have dimmed Ameritech's prospects.
The Justice Department must issue a recommendation to the FCC by February 21.

In a news release, the MPSC said that in a 2-1 vote among commissioners the agency authorized the filing of comments with the FCC. In its comments, the agency said it appears that Ameritech's Michigan unit has met the technical requirements of the checklist.
"For many years, the Michigan Public Service Commission has supported allowing expanded choice for telephone customers," said MPSC Chairman John Strand.
"Our comments today are designed to assist the Federal Communications Commission to follow a course that will introduce more competition in the telecommunications marketplace."

Ameritech filed its initial request with the FCC to provide long-distance service from Michigan on January 2. The carrier later was forced to amend its filing with an additional 1,500 pages of documents after regulators determined that many needed pages were missing.
Long-distance giants AT&T Corp. and MCI Communications Corp have called on regulators to reject Ameritech's request, saying that the company has not yet opened its local market fully to competitors.
